examples.en: Two strong teams clash in today's final.
The two candidates clashed head-on in the debate.

examples.ko: 의견이 달라서 회의 때 격돌하기도 해요.
examples.en: Because our opinions differ, we sometimes clash in meetings.
The teams that will clash for the title have been decided.
I'm nervous because we have to face our rival team.

examples.ko: 결승에서 격돌했던 두 선수가 다시 만났어요.
examples.en: The two players who clashed in the final met again.

explain: 'A와 B가 격돌하다'나 'A가 B와 격돌하다' 모양으로 써요. 일상에서는 '맞붙다'가 더 편하고, '격돌하다'는 기사나 중계에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 내일 우리 반이 옆 반과 맞붙어요.
phrases.en: Tomorrow our class will go head to head with the next class.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more casual and common in daily speech than 격돌하다.

phrases.example: 두 회사가 새 시장에서 정면으로 격돌해요.
phrases.en: The two companies clash head-on in the new market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피하지 않고 크게 부딪치는 모습을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes colliding big without backing away.

phrases.example: 두 팀이 격돌한 끝에 무승부로 끝났어요.
phrases.en: After the two teams clashed, it ended in a draw.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치열하게 맞붙은 뒤의 결과를 말할 때 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to lead into the result after a fierce clash.

explain_en: It is used as 'A와 B가 격돌하다' or 'A가 B와 격돌하다'. In daily talk '맞붙다' (to go head to head) is more casual, while '격돌하다' shows up more in articles and match commentary.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 두 팀의 맞대결이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a head-to-head match between the two teams this evening.

examples.ko: 형과 저는 게임에서 자주 맞대결을 해요.
examples.en: My brother and I often have showdowns in games.
I really want to win this showdown.

examples.ko: 두 가수의 맞대결이 큰 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The face-off between the two singers became a big topic.
I was curious about the result, so I waited all night.
Old rivals face off in the final.

explain: 맞대결은 두 상대가 서로 정면으로 겨루는 거예요. 경기에서 '대결'만 쓰면 일반적인 겨루기이고, '맞'이 붙으면 힘이 비슷한 둘이 직접 마주한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '맞대결을 펼치다', '맞대결을 벌이다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The two players face off head-to-head in the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 경기 소식에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used in news and sports reports.

phrases.example: 오늘 맞대결 상대는 작년 우승 팀이에요.
phrases.en: Today's head-to-head opponent is last year's champion.
The two teams will go head-to-head this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맞대결'과 비슷한 뜻의 동사로 말할 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb with a meaning close to 맞대결, handy in speech.

explain_en: 맞대결 is two opponents going straight at each other. Plain 대결 is general competing, but adding 맞 gives more of a feeling that two evenly matched sides face off directly. It usually appears as 맞대결을 펼치다 or 맞대결을 벌이다.

examples.en: As soon as it was released, this film was called a controversial work.

examples.ko: 그 감독의 문제작을 이번 주말에 볼 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to watch that director's provocative film this weekend.
It's a novel that sparked a lot of debate because it was so provocative.
I watched a drama that was rated as a work that stirred controversy.

examples.ko: 올해 가장 큰 문제작은 뭐라고 생각해요?
examples.en: What do you think is this year's most talked-about provocative work?

examples.ko: 문제작이 나올 때마다 신문에 비평이 실려요.
examples.en: Every time a provocative work comes out, reviews appear in the newspaper.

explain: 작품에 문제가 있다는 뜻이 아니라, 화제와 논란을 일으켰다는 말이에요. 비판도 받지만 그만큼 주목할 만한 작품이라는 느낌이 있고, '화제작'은 논란보다 이야깃거리가 된 작품을 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 소설은 올해 최고의 문제작으로 꼽혀요.
phrases.en: This novel is ranked as the most controversial work of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 화제로 삼는 작품으로 손꼽힌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a work is singled out as one that caused a stir.
phrases.en_equiv: to be ranked as a controversial work

phrases.en: That director released a new controversial work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 논란이 될 만한 작품을 내놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone releases a work likely to cause debate.

phrases.en: This drama is truly a controversial work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품이 화제와 논란을 일으켰다고 말하는 해요체 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite-style statement that a work has caused buzz and debate.

explain_en: It does not mean the work is flawed; it means the work stirred talk and controversy. It carries a sense of being worth attention despite criticism, while '화제작' just means a work people are talking about.

examples.en: The second half of the game will be the deciding stretch.
A player who doesn't slip up at the crucial moment is strong.
The last three minutes were the turning point of this game.
In the election, the Seoul metropolitan area is seen as the key battleground.
In this negotiation, price is the deciding factor.
That player had the ball at every crucial moment.

explain: 실제 전쟁터가 아니라 경기나 선거에서 승패가 갈리는 결정적인 순간이나 지역을 말해요. 스포츠 중계와 선거 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. '승부처에서 강하다'처럼 사람의 능력을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 이번 선거는 서울이 승부처가 될 거예요.
phrases.en: In this election, Seoul will be the decisive battleground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 시간이나 지역이 결과를 정하는 곳이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a certain time or place will decide the outcome.

phrases.en: That player is really strong in crunch time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 순간에 실력을 잘 내는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praises someone who performs well at critical moments.

phrases.en: The fourth quarter is the biggest turning point of this game.
phrases.nuance_ko: '최대'를 붙여 가장 중요한 순간이나 곳을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 최대 stresses the single most important moment or place.

explain_en: It isn't a literal battlefield; it is the decisive moment or place where a game or election is won or lost. You hear it in sports commentary and election news. It is also used to describe a person's strength, as in '승부처에서 강하다'.

examples.ko: 두 팀은 경기 전부터 심리전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two teams played mind games even before the match.
Negotiation is ultimately a mind game.

examples.ko: 감독이 일부러 말을 아끼는 것도 심리전일 수 있어요.
examples.en: The coach deliberately saying little could also be a mind game.
In baduk, mind games matter as well as skill.
You shouldn't get drawn into the opponent's mind games.

examples.ko: 요즘 두 회사 사이에 심리전이 치열해요.
examples.en: Mind games between the two companies are intense these days.

explain: 심리전은 상대의 마음을 흔들어서 유리해지려는 싸움이에요. 스포츠, 협상, 정치 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 같은 뜻으로 일상에서는 '기 싸움'을 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 두 선수가 경기 전에 심리전을 벌였어요.
phrases.en: The two players played mind games before the match.
phrases.nuance_en: Means both sides try to rattle each other.

phrases.en: An intense mind game continued in the negotiation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심리전이 아주 센 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the mind game is very intense.

phrases.example: 둘이 서로 지지 않으려고 기 싸움을 해요.
phrases.en: The two refuse to lose and are in a battle of wills.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, '기 싸움' is said more often than '심리전'.

explain_en: 심리전 is a contest of shaking the other side's mind to gain an edge. It appears often in sports, negotiation and politics. In everyday speech '기 싸움' is used a lot for a similar idea.
